findings.pdf_says: 12.4.6.3.2 General format:  APPLY COMMIT ON  [[ file-name-1][identifier-1]]...   — in the printed figure APPLY and COMMIT each carry an underline; ON carries no underline. (Preceding figure, 12.4.6.2: "I-O-CONTROL  .  [ [ apply-commit-clause] . ]   [[{ same-clause }...].]" — I-O-CONTROL is underlined.)
findings.markdown_says:
```
APPLY COMMIT ON  [[ file-name-1][identifier-1]]…
```
(and, above it, "```\nI-O-CONTROL . [ [ apply-commit-clause] . ]  [[ { same-clause } …].]\n```") — both figures are plain code blocks with no <u> markup and no "Figure notes" paragraph, so no underlining information survives.
findings.why_it_matters: Underlining is normative in a general format: underlined uppercase words are required words, non-underlined uppercase words are optional words. With the underlines dropped, the markdown APPLY COMMIT ON reads as three required keywords, when ON is optional — the falsely-restrictive-syntax failure mode this sweep is hunting. Every other general format in this batch preserves the distinction: pages 349, 355, 357, 359, 361 and 365 each carry an explicit "Figure notes" paragraph naming which words are underlined, and page 365 Formats 1 and 2 use inline <u>SAME</u> / <u>RECORD</u> markup. Page 363 is the only figure-bearing page in the batch that records neither.
findings.suggested_repair: Add a "Figure notes" paragraph after each of the two code blocks on page 363, matching the convention used on 349/355/357/359/361/365: for 12.4.6.3.2 state that APPLY and COMMIT are underlined (required words) and ON is not underlined (optional word), and that the ellipsis binds to the outer bracket pair so the [ file-name-1 ][ identifier-1 ] group may repeat; for 12.4.6.2 state that I-O-CONTROL is underlined and that nothing else in that figure is.
